resources.string: Select a distortion type (only one at a time):
Ready. Select a distortion type and tap "Apply Distortion and Evaluate".
Generating distortion and computing objective metrics…

"Distortion: %1$s

MSE: %2$.2f (mean squared error, Eq. 9-2)
MAE: %3$.2f (mean absolute error, Eq. 9-1)
PSNR: %4$.2f dB (peak signal-to-noise ratio, Eq. 9-3)
SSIM: %5$.4f (structural similarity, Eq. 9-4)
Entropy (original): %6$.3f bit/px
Entropy (distorted): %7$.3f bit/px

Quality grade: %8$s"
Excellent (PSNR≥40dB and SSIM≥0.95, distortion nearly imperceptible)
Good (PSNR 30~40dB and SSIM 0.85~0.95, perceptible but not objectionable)
Fair (PSNR 20~30dB and SSIM 0.60~0.85, clearly visible distortion)
Poor (PSNR below 20dB or SSIM below 0.60, severe distortion)

"【Distortion】Lossy JPEG compression (quality Q=10, Ch. 5): 8×8 blocks → DCT transform → coarse quantization (most high-frequency coefficients zeroed — the root of information loss) → entropy coding. The reconstructed image shows blocking artifacts and ringing; high-frequency detail is lost.\n【Evaluation】PSNR/SSIM drop significantly; entropy (information) decreases with lost detail."

"【Distortion】Additive white Gaussian noise (σ=15): each pixel receives an N(0,σ²) random perturbation, modeling acquisition/transmission noise.\n【Evaluation】MSE rises uniformly, PSNR ≈ 24~25dB; SSIM drops as local structures are corrupted; entropy rises as the histogram widens."

"【Distortion】Salt-and-pepper noise (density 5%%): pixels randomly forced to 0 (pepper) or 255 (salt), modeling impulse interference.\n【Evaluation】A few pixels are grossly wrong → large MSE and low PSNR; but most pixels are intact, so SSIM degrades less than MSE suggests — showing SSIM is sensitive to structural distortion yet relatively tolerant of isolated outliers."

"【Distortion】3×3 mean filtering (low-pass blur): high-frequency detail attenuated, modeling defocus.\n【Evaluation】MSE rises, but more importantly the structure/contrast factors of SSIM drop sharply — blur preserves mean luminance yet destroys edges and texture; SSIM reflects this subjective loss better than PSNR."

"【Distortion】Brightness shift (Δ=+30): a constant added to all pixels; contrast and structure (high-frequency content) unchanged.\n【Evaluation】MSE=Δ²=900 (PSNR≈18.6dB, very low), yet only the luminance factor l of SSIM drops while contrast and structure factors stay 1 — the textbook conclusion: PSNR may disagree with perceived quality, while SSIM matches human perception better."

"【Objective evaluation】(Ch. 9, 9.2~9.4) Objective evaluation measures image quality with mathematical models, without human scoring (subjective MOS). Full-reference evaluation requires both the original image f and the distorted image g:
【Eq. 9-1】MAE = (1/MN)·ΣΣ|f(i,j)−g(i,j)|
【Eq. 9-2】MSE = (1/MN)·ΣΣ[f(i,j)−g(i,j)]²
【Eq. 9-3】PSNR = 10·lg(L²/MSE), L=255 (8bit), in dB; higher PSNR means less distortion (>40dB is usually imperceptible).
【Eq. 9-4】SSIM(x,y) = [l(x,y)]^α·[c(x,y)]^β·[s(x,y)]^γ
【Eq. 9-5】l=(2μxμy+C1)/(μx²+μy²+C1) (luminance)
 c=(2σxσy+C2)/(σx²+σy²+C2) (contrast)
 s=(σxy+C3)/(σxσy+C3) (structure), C1=(0.01L)², C2=(0.03L)², C3=C2/2
【Eq. 9-6】Here α=β=γ=1; SSIM is computed over 8×8 blocks and averaged over the image; SSIM∈(0,1], closer to 1 means more similar structure.
【Entropy】H = −Σ p(i)·log₂p(i) (bit/px), measures information content.
【Pipeline】Decode the assets image → extract luminance Y → apply the selected distortion → compute all metrics → comparison display and grade."
Select a target bitrate (only one at a time):
Ready. Select a target bitrate and tap "Transcode and Evaluate Per-frame". Lower bitrate gives higher compression and lower PSNR/SSIM (rate-distortion trade-off).
Phase 2: dual decoding, computing per-frame PSNR / SSIM…
Result (middle frame comparison: original vs compressed)

"Target bitrate: %1$.1f Mbps

Average PSNR: %2$.2f dB (over all frames)
Worst-frame PSNR: %3$.2f dB (frame %4$d)
Average SSIM: %5$.4f
Worst-frame SSIM: %6$.4f

Original size: %7$.2f MB
Compressed size: %8$.2f MB
Compression ratio: %9$.1f : 1

Frames evaluated: %11$d
Elapsed: %10$.1f s"

"【Video quality evaluation】(Ch. 9 + Ch. 5/6/7) A video is an image sequence; objective evaluation is based on per-frame full-reference metrics plus temporal aggregation: PSNR (Eq. 9-3) and SSIM (Eq. 9-4~9-6) are computed on the luminance plane of every frame of the original x(n) and compressed y(n), then averaged over all frames, with the worst frame (quality floor) also reported.
【Rate-distortion R-D】(Ch. 5, 5.5 / Ch. 6): rate R and distortion D constrain each other in lossy compression — lower R (4Mbps→256kbps) → larger quantization step → higher D (lower PSNR/SSIM). The H.264 encoder (Ch. 6) controls the bitrate via intra prediction, motion-compensated inter prediction, transform+quantization and entropy coding; the MP4 container (Ch. 7) packages the bitstream.
【Pipeline】assets/video.mp4 → H.264 transcode at the selected bitrate (phase 1) → dual decode of original/compressed videos with per-frame evaluation (phase 2: PSNR at full resolution, SSIM on 2× downsampled luma for speed) → average/worst-frame metrics, compression ratio and middle-frame comparison.
【Verification】Evaluate at 4Mbps / 1Mbps / 256kbps in turn and observe PSNR/SSIM decreasing monotonically while the compression ratio increases — a direct verification of rate-distortion theory."
